Data Wrangling

Dataframe filters to check for sample size

# Filter for no aide
had_aide <- df_students$gkclasstype == 3 | 
  df_students$g1classtype == 3 | 
  df_students$g2classtype == 3 | 
  df_students$g3classtype == 3

df_students_noaide <- df_students[!had_aide,]
nrow(df_students_noaide)
## [1] 6307
# Filter for no aide and were in study all 4 years
df_students_noaide_4years <- df_students[!had_aide &
                                         !is.na(df_students$gkclasstype) & 
                                         !is.na(df_students$g1classtype) & 
                                         !is.na(df_students$g2classtype) & 
                                         !is.na(df_students$g3classtype), ]

nrow(df_students_noaide_4years)

The subset of all small and all regular has good sample size. The subsets of regular to small (rrrs, rrss, rsss) are also sufficient in which we could compare if multiple years leads to higher scores and we could comapre 3rd grade. However subsetting For the other way around small to regular (srrr, ssrr, sssr), the sample is lower.

Class Type “Trend” Groups

# initalize trend column
df_students_noaide_4years$trend_all <- "Other"

# move column
df_students_noaide_4years <- df_students_noaide_4years %>% 
  relocate(trend_all, .before = class_group) 
# Change class trend groups for each student

# All 4 years of small vs regular has enough sample size so we can keep those the same
df_students_noaide_4years$trend_all[df_students_noaide_4years$class_group == "ssss"] <- "constant_small"
df_students_noaide_4years$trend_all[df_students_noaide_4years$class_group == "rrrr"] <- "constant_reg"

# Small to regular trend (srrr, ssrr, sssr)
subset <- c('srrr', 'ssrr', 'sssr')
df_students_noaide_4years$trend_all[df_students_noaide_4years$class_group %in% subset] <- "small_to_reg"

# Regular to small trend (rsss, rrss, rrrs)
subset <- c('rsss', 'rrss', 'rrrs')
df_students_noaide_4years$trend_all[df_students_noaide_4years$class_group %in% subset] <- "reg_to_small"

Factor Labels

# Set factors and labels

# Urban and free lunch variables for question 1 
df_students_noaide_4years$gksurban <- factor(df_students_noaide_4years$gksurban, labels = c("Inner City", "Suburban", "Rural", "Urban")) # urban


# Gender, race, and free lunch variables for question 2
df_students_noaide_4years$gender <- factor(df_students_noaide_4years$gender, labels = c("Male", "Female")) # gender

df_students_noaide_4years <- subset(df_students_noaide_4years, race %in% c(1,2)) # subset for white and black only
df_students_noaide_4years$race <- factor(df_students_noaide_4years$race, labels = c("White", "Black")) # race

df_students_noaide_4years$g3freelunch <- factor(df_students_noaide_4years$g3freelunch, labels = c("Free", "Non-Free")) # free lunch for grade 3
df_students_noaide_4years$gkfreelunch <- factor(df_students_noaide_4years$gkfreelunch, labels = c("Free", "Non-Free")) # free lunch for kindergarten
nrow(df_students_noaide_4years)
## [1] 1426

Early Year Class Size vs Socioeconomic (Question 1)

Three Way Anova Model

# Urbanicity + free lunch
model_fixed1 <- aov(gktmathss ~ gkclasstype + gkfreelunch + gksurban, data = df_students_noaide_4years)
model_fixed2 <- aov(gktmathss ~ gkclasstype * gkfreelunch + gksurban, data = df_students_noaide_4years)
model_fixed3 <- aov(gktmathss ~ gkclasstype * gksurban + gkfreelunch, data = df_students_noaide_4years)
model_fixed4 <- aov(gktmathss ~ gkclasstype * gksurban * gkfreelunch, data = df_students_noaide_4years)
summary(model_fixed1)

Model equation $$ Y_{ijkl} = + _i + _j + k + {ijkl} \

\ _i \ _j \ k \ {ijkl} N(0, ^2) $$

AIC(model_fixed1, model_fixed2, model_fixed3, model_fixed4)
##              df      AIC
## model_fixed1  7 13990.23
## model_fixed2  8 13992.21
## model_fixed3 10 13995.79
## model_fixed4 17 14004.46
BIC(model_fixed1, model_fixed2, model_fixed3, model_fixed4)
##              df      BIC
## model_fixed1  7 14026.64
## model_fixed2  8 14033.82
## model_fixed3 10 14047.81
## model_fixed4 17 14092.90
anova(model_fixed1, model_fixed2, model_fixed3, model_fixed4) 
## Analysis of Variance Table
## 
## Model 1: gktmathss ~ gkclasstype + gkfreelunch + gksurban
## Model 2: gktmathss ~ gkclasstype * gkfreelunch + gksurban
## Model 3: gktmathss ~ gkclasstype * gksurban + gkfreelunch
## Model 4: gktmathss ~ gkclasstype * gksurban * gkfreelunch
##   Res.Df     RSS Df Sum of Sq      F Pr(>F)
## 1   1336 2619558                           
## 2   1335 2619513  1      44.9 0.0228 0.8799
## 3   1333 2618711  2     802.4 0.2040 0.8155
## 4   1326 2608328  7   10382.6 0.7540 0.6261
# Table df
f_table <- data.frame(
  'Model' = c("Additive", "Interaction (classsize*freelunch)", "Interaction (classsize*urbanicity)", "Interaction (classsize*freelunch*urbanicity)"),
  'Parameters' = c("8", "9", "11", "18"),
  'Residual df' = c("1336", "1335", "1333", "1326"), 
  'AIC' = c("13990", "13992", "13996", "14004"),
  'BIC' = c("14026", "14034", "14048", "14093"),
  'RSS' = c("2619558", "2619513", "2618711", "2608328"),
  'Sum Sq.' = c("", "44.9", "802.4", "10382.6"),
  'F-stat.' = c("", "0.0228", "0.2040", "0.7540"),
  'p-val.' = c("", "0.8799", "0.8155", "0.6261"),
  check.names = FALSE
)

# Create table
kable(f_table, 
      caption = "Table 2: Comparison of Three-way ANOVA Candidate Models by F Test", 
      align = c('l', 'l', 'l', 'l')) %>%
kable_classic(full_width = T, html_font = "Cambria")

Looking at Switch (Question 2)

Small class pattern

# if we are examining grade 3 math, we have to look at students of similar groups
# Subset for groups of interest: Compliers (constant class size) and Noncompliers (switch)
subset <- c('rsss', 'rrss', 'rrrs', 'rrrr', 'ssss', 'srrr', 'ssrr', 'sssr')
df <- df_students_noaide_4years[df_students_noaide_4years$class_group %in% subset, ] 

nrow(df)
## [1] 1407
table(df$trend_all)
## 
##   constant_reg constant_small   reg_to_small   small_to_reg 
##            365            853            151             38
# Table df
trend_table <- data.frame(
  'Trend' = c("Constant Regular Class Size", "Constant Small Class Size", "Regular to Small Class Size", "Small to Regular Class Size", "Total"),
  'Sample Size' = c("365", "853", "151", "38", "1407"),
  check.names = FALSE
)

# Create table
kable(trend_table, 
      caption = "Table 1: Trend Variable Sample Size post Filter", 
      align = c('l', 'l', 'l', 'l')) %>%
  kable_classic(full_width = F, html_font = "Cambria") %>%
  row_spec(5, bold = T, extra_css = "border-top: 1px solid black;")

##     step
# Baselines are constant regular class size, white, male, non-free lunch and teacher experience included


# Mixed effects model where school is random intercept examining trend variable
model_mixed1 <- lmer(g3tmathss ~ trend_all + gender + race + g3freelunch + g3tyears + (1 | g3schid), data = df) # additive
model_mixed2 <- lmer(g3tmathss ~ trend_all * g3freelunch + gender + race + g3tyears + (1 | g3schid), data = df) # interaction trend * lunch
model_mixed3 <- lmer(g3tmathss ~ trend_all * race + gender + g3freelunch + g3tyears + (1 | g3schid), data = df) # interaction trend * race

Model equation $$ Y_{ij} = _0 + _1 + _2 + _3 + 4 + 5 + b{0j}+ {ij}

\ b_{0j} N(0, ^2_b)\ \ _{ij} N(0, ^2) $$

# Looking at larger dataset so use BIC for parsomonious model
BIC(model_mixed1, model_mixed2, model_mixed3)
##              df      BIC
## model_mixed1 10 12954.50
## model_mixed2 13 12950.55
## model_mixed3 13 12955.48
# Likelihood ratio test
anova(model_mixed1, model_mixed2)
## refitting model(s) with ML (instead of REML)
## Data: df
## Models:
## model_mixed1: g3tmathss ~ trend_all + gender + race + g3freelunch + g3tyears + (1 | g3schid)
## model_mixed2: g3tmathss ~ trend_all * g3freelunch + gender + race + g3tyears + (1 | g3schid)
##              npar   AIC   BIC  logLik -2*log(L)  Chisq Df Pr(>Chisq)  
## model_mixed1   10 12928 12980 -6454.2     12908                       
## model_mixed2   13 12927 12994 -6450.3     12901 7.7188  3     0.0522 .
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
anova(model_mixed1, model_mixed3)
## refitting model(s) with ML (instead of REML)
## Data: df
## Models:
## model_mixed1: g3tmathss ~ trend_all + gender + race + g3freelunch + g3tyears + (1 | g3schid)
## model_mixed3: g3tmathss ~ trend_all * race + gender + g3freelunch + g3tyears + (1 | g3schid)
##              npar   AIC   BIC  logLik -2*log(L)  Chisq Df Pr(>Chisq)
## model_mixed1   10 12928 12980 -6454.2     12908                     
## model_mixed3   13 12932 12999 -6453.1     12906 2.1038  3     0.5511
# Table df
lrt_table <- data.frame(
  'Model' = c("Additive", "Interaction (trend*freelunch)", "Interaction (trend*race)"),
  'Parameters' = c("10", "13", "13"),
  'AIC' = c("12928", "12927", "12980"),
  'BIC' = c("12980", "12994", "12999"),
  '-2log(L)' = c("12908", "12901", "12906"), 
  'Chisq' = c("", "7.7188", "2.1038"),
  'p-value' = c("", "0.0522", "0.5511"),
  check.names = FALSE
)

# Create table
kable(lrt_table, 
      caption = "Table 3: Comparison of Mixed Effects Candidate Models by Likelihood Ratio Test", 
      align = c('l', 'l', 'l', 'l')) %>%
kable_classic(full_width = F, html_font = "Cambria")
Table 3: Comparison of Mixed Effects Candidate Models by Likelihood Ratio Test
Model Parameters AIC BIC -2log(L) Chisq p-value
Additive 10 12928 12980 12908
Interaction (trend*freelunch) 13 12927 12994 12901 7.7188 0.0522
Interaction (trend*race) 13 12980 12999 12906 2.1038 0.5511

Although the interactions model with lunch had a slightly lower BIC, the likelihood ratio test was not significant indicating the additive model is sufficient.

Noncomplier Random (prob scrap)

# Compares baselines in kindergarden between compliers and non-compliers  
t.test(gktmathss ~ trend_all, data = subset(df, trend_all %in% c("constant_reg", "reg_to_small"))) 
## 
##  Welch Two Sample t-test
## 
## data:  gktmathss by trend_all
## t = -1.2523, df = 237.06, p-value = 0.2117
## alternative hypothesis: true difference in means between group constant_reg and group reg_to_small is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  -14.629168   3.258342
## sample estimates:
## mean in group constant_reg mean in group reg_to_small 
##                   492.1965                   497.8819
t.test(gktmathss ~ trend_all, data = subset(df, trend_all %in% c("constant_small", "small_to_reg"))) 
## 
##  Welch Two Sample t-test
## 
## data:  gktmathss by trend_all
## t = 1.4978, df = 35.024, p-value = 0.1432
## alternative hypothesis: true difference in means between group constant_small and group small_to_reg is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  -4.11044 27.24253
## sample estimates:
## mean in group constant_small   mean in group small_to_reg 
##                     505.8994                     494.3333

Sensitivity Analysis

Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC)

# ICC for trend model
var_comp <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(model_mixed1))
v_school <- var_comp$vcov[1]
v_residual <- var_comp$vcov[2]

v_school / (v_school + v_residual)
## [1] 0.1356374

Around 13.56% of student’s score is due to school effects when considered the model for trend
